title: GDScript LSP ignores $/cancelRequest, so expensive requests can block subsequent requests
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot 4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4].
- Current `master` source at `5ec4857b340b6284a18b49b2eda462bd250f219a` was audited as well: `textDocument/references` still uses the project-wide `find_all_usages` path, and no `$/cancelRequest` handler is present in the repository.

### System information

Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, build 26200 - Godot 4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4]

### Issue description

The GDScript language server does not handle the LSP `$/cancelRequest` notification. This becomes visible when an expensive request such as `textDocument/references` is issued in a large GDScript workspace.

In our reproducible project (1,315 `.gd` files total, 1,019 under the main scripts directory), a non-local `textDocument/references` request can run long enough for the client to time out after 60 seconds. Cancelling the request client-side does not stop the server-side work, and a following lightweight request such as `textDocument/documentSymbol` can then time out as well because the language server is still occupied.

Current `master` still routes references through `GDScriptWorkspace::find_all_usages`, which scans scripts under `res://` for non-local symbols:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5ec4857b340b6284a18b49b2eda462bd250f219a/modules/gdscript/language_server/gdscript_text_document.cpp

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5ec4857b340b6284a18b49b2eda462bd250f219a/modules/gdscript/language_server/gdscript_workspace.cpp

The current language-protocol implementation also has no `$/cancelRequest` handling:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5ec4857b340b6284a18b49b2eda462bd250f219a/modules/gdscript/language_server/gdscript_language_protocol.cpp

A repository search for `cancelRequest` at that `master` revision returns no implementation.
Related work: #114729 and PR #115851 improved a `find_all_usages` slowdown/crash case, especially for short identifiers. This report is about the separate cancellation/responsiveness problem: once a long LSP request is in progress, the client cannot cancel that server-side work.

Expected behavior: when the client sends `$/cancelRequest` for a long-running request, Godot should stop that request as soon as practical and keep the language server responsive to subsequent requests.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a sufficiently large GDScript project in Godot 4.6.3 with the language server enabled.
2. Connect an LSP client and initialize normally.
3. Send `textDocument/references` for a non-local symbol that causes a workspace-wide reference search.
4. While the request is still running, send the standard LSP notification:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"$/cancelRequest","params":{"id":<references-request-id>}}
```

5. Immediately send a lightweight request such as `textDocument/documentSymbol`.
6. Observe that the reference search continues server-side and the following request remains blocked; in our reproduction both the original references request and the subsequent document-symbol request reached the client's 60-second timeout.

The exact runtime duration depends on workspace size and symbol frequency, but the underlying cancellation gap is visible directly in the current source because there is no `$/cancelRequest` handler.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Not attached yet. The issue reproduces in a large existing GDScript workspace. A synthetic large-workspace MRP can be provided if needed; the current-source absence of any `$/cancelRequest` handler is independent of project content.
